prerequisites.reason: The effort level determines the strength of the penalty coefficient.
Penalty strength dictates the preferred reasoning length during optimization.

mechanisms.statement: Raising reasoning effort scales output length predictably by decaying the token penalty coefficient exponentially.
Increased reasoning length improves accuracy as long as the marginal benefit of additional tokens remains positive.

claims.statement: Raising effort from 25 to 100 scales average response length by 2.0–3.1× across benchmarks.
The predictable scaling of tokens allows compute costs for any effort tier to be estimated in advance.
Accuracy responds positively or remains stable as effort increases, with no observed degradation.

terminology.definition: Scalar k(b) controlling pressure toward shorter reasoning based on effort level b.
